Revised assessment (with SLOOS): The FOMC’s cautiously accommodative stance—grounded in solid employment but below-target inflation—remains appropriate. However, the latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to a softer private credit impulse: banks reported weaker demand across CRE (including construction, land development, and multifamily) and consumer credit (auto and credit cards), alongside tighter standards for consumer, auto, and credit card loans. While standards eased for residential mortgages (including jumbo, QM, and GSE), overall demand in several sectors softened. Foreign banks reported tighter standards for C&I and CRE even as they saw some strengthening in CRE demand. These SLOOS signals imply downside risks to growth and inflation from credit channels, reinforcing Fed patience and gradualism and limiting the case for near-term tightening. Balance-sheet normalization “relatively soon” remains a mild hawkish note, but with limited immediate restraint on financial conditions. Net tone: modestly positive for duration and only mildly positive for risk assets, tempered by weaker credit demand/tighter consumer standards.

Updated excerpt: “Job gains are solid and inflation is soft, and the Fed signals patience with rates below neutral for some time; SLOOS shows weaker loan demand and tighter consumer credit standards, underscoring a cautious growth outlook.”
